title: Temporal Knowledge Graph
lead: Entity→predicate→entity facts with validity windows, stored in local SQLite and queryable by time.
summary: The Temporal Knowledge Graph stores structured facts as subject→predicate→object triples with optional valid_from/valid_to timestamps, enabling queries at specific points in time. Built on SQLite with thread-safe WAL mode and no external dependencies, it complements vector search by providing deterministic relationship queries ("Who was Alice's employer in 2023?") and serves as ground truth for fact-checking and entity disambiguation.

concepts.definition: A fact expressed as subject→predicate→object (e.g., 'Alice' → 'works_at' → 'Acme Corp'). The core KG unit; predicates are normalized to lowercase and underscores.

Optional valid_from/valid_to timestamps defining when a fact is true. Both can be ISO-8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD) or canonical UTC datetimes (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). NULL means unbounded; values are inclusive on both ends.

A query parameter returning only facts valid at a specified instant. Date-only queries like 'as_of=2026-01-15' normalize to 'T00:00:00Z'; the comparison logic handles legacy date-only values and canonical UTC datetimes.
Closing a fact by setting its valid_to date. The original triple with NULL valid_to is updated to have an ended timestamp; no rows are deleted, preserving audit trail and time-travel queries.

Person/project/concept nodes identified by lowercase-slugified names (entity_id). The registry in entity_registry.py and fact_checker.py detect duplicates and confusion; the KG enforces deterministic lookups via this slug.
Optional source_drawer_id, adapter_name, source_closet, and source_file track where a fact came from — the drawer that mentions it, the adapter that extracted it, or the file/closet it references.
A per-triple float (default 1.0) indicating certainty. Currently not used in ranking but reserved for future fact-assessment integrations and conflict resolution.
A chronologically sorted view of facts for an entity or across the entire KG, ordered by valid_from (NULL values last). Limited to 100 rows; useful for narrative reconstruction.

symbols.name: KnowledgeGraph
symbols.role: Main KG interface. Manages SQLite connection, locking, and all read/write operations. Singleton per palace path, cached in mcp_server._kg_by_path.

symbols.name: add_triple
symbols.role: Primary write operation for facts. Auto-creates entities, validates intervals, deduplicates on subject/predicate/object + valid_to IS NULL, generates unique triple_id.

symbols.name: query_entity
symbols.role: Primary read operation. Returns all facts for an entity, optionally at a specific as_of moment, in a given direction (outgoing/incoming/both).

symbols.name: invalidate
symbols.role: Closes an open fact by setting valid_to. Validates that ended >= valid_from. Idempotent if called multiple times.

symbols.name: _temporal_filter_sql
symbols.role: Generates the WHERE clause for temporal queries. Handles date-only and canonical UTC normalization via CASE expressions.

symbols.name: timeline
symbols.role: Returns facts in chronological order, optionally for a single entity. Limited to 100 rows. Useful for narrative reconstruction.

symbols.name: seed_from_entity_facts
symbols.role: Bootstrap method to populate the KG from a dict of curated facts (used in tests and initial setup). Handles relationships, interests, and entity metadata.

symbols.name: tool_kg_query
symbols.role: MCP server interface for querying the KG. Sanitizes inputs and calls query_entity via _call_kg.

symbols.name: tool_kg_add
symbols.role: MCP server interface for adding triples. Logs to WAL, sanitizes inputs, forwards to add_triple.

symbols.name: _call_kg
symbols.role: Helper that acquires the per-path KG singleton and calls a lambda. Ensures single writer, consistent reads.

symbols.name: check_text
symbols.role: Fact-checking entrypoint. Validates incoming text against KG for contradictions (stale_fact, relationship_mismatch) and entity confusions.

symbols.name: sanitize_iso_temporal
symbols.role: Validator for temporal parameters. Rejects partial dates and non-UTC timezones. Normalizes +00:00 to Z. Used at MCP boundary for all temporal inputs.

surprises.title: Date-only facts are interpreted as full-day intervals at query time
surprises.detail: Legacy triples stored with valid_from='2026-01-01' (no time) are normalized to '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' at query time, while valid_to='2026-01-01' becomes '2026-01-01T23:59:59Z'. This allows as_of queries using canonical UTC datetimes (e.g., '2026-01-15T10:30:00Z') to still match date-only facts. The trick is in _temporal_start_key and _temporal_end_key functions and their SQL equivalents, which treat a date as a 24-hour window rather than a point.

surprises.title: Invalidation is idempotent: calling it twice on the same fact is safe
surprises.detail: The invalidate method searches for triples with valid_to IS NULL (line 340). If called twice on the same fact, the second call finds no matches and does nothing, which is semantically correct but might surprise callers expecting an error. The implementation is forgiving, which aligns with CLAUDE.md's 'incremental-only' principle—operations are replay-safe.

surprises.title: Predicates are always lowercased and space→underscore normalized
surprises.detail: When adding a triple, predicates are normalized to lowercase with underscores (line 282). This means 'Child Of', 'child_of', and 'CHILD_OF' all map to the same predicate. This is intentional (simplifies predicate discovery), but callers expecting case preservation will be surprised.

surprises.title: The KG does NOT enforce referential integrity at write time
surprises.detail: Although the schema declares FOREIGN KEY (subject) REFERENCES entities(id), the KG auto-creates missing entities on-the-fly (lines 288–295). This means you can add a triple for entities that don't yet exist. The foreign key constraint is a soft constraint (no immediate error), but it documents the intent. This is intentional: it allows flexible triple creation without pre-populating the entity table.

surprises.title: Timeline queries are limited to 100 rows; if you have more, they are silently truncated
surprises.detail: The timeline method (line 476) uses LIMIT 100, which is a reasonable default for interactive queries but can silently hide facts if your timeline exceeds 100 entries. There is no pagination mechanism; a follow-up query or API design change would be needed for larger timelines.

designDecisions.decision: SQLite over Neo4j or other graph database
designDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md principle: 'Local-first, zero external API'. Neo4j (like Zep's offering) requires a running server or cloud subscription ($25/month+). SQLite is zero-infrastructure, file-based, and embedded. It sacrifices graph traversal performance (no native graph indexes) for simplicity, fit-for-purpose trade-off given MemPalace workloads (entity stars, not deep graph navigation).

designDecisions.decision: Thread-safe with a single lock + WAL mode, not optimistic concurrency
designDecisions.rationale: MCP server is single-process with background hooks running in threads. A coarse lock is simpler and sufficient; fine-grained locking would add complexity without benefit. WAL mode enables concurrent reads while writes hold the lock, and the 10-second timeout tolerates occasional contention from heavy indexing or search operations.

designDecisions.decision: Normalize predicates to lowercase/underscores at write time, not query time
designDecisions.rationale: Simplicity and consistency. By normalizing on insert, queries don't need case-insensitive matchers. The downside (loss of original casing) is acceptable because relationships are typically written by code, not user input, and semantic normalization (parent, parent_of, ParentOf → parent_of) is more valuable than fidelity.

designDecisions.decision: Temporal comparisons use SQL CASE expressions, not Python normalization
designDecisions.rationale: Performance and correctness. Normalizing in SQL means comparisons happen once per query, over the actual stored values, avoiding redundant conversions and keeping the code path close to the data. Date-only facts are normalized just-in-time (23:59:59 for valid_to, 00:00:00 for valid_from), preserving the intent that a date spans the full day.

designDecisions.decision: Invalidation updates the same row (set valid_to), rather than inserting a new row with the end date
designDecisions.rationale: Audit trail and correctness. Updating valid_to preserves the original triple ID and maintains a single version of the fact, with its full lifetime visible in one row. If we inserted a new row with 'ended' semantics, queries would become more complex (UNION of 'version 1 valid until X' and 'version 2 starts after X'). Update is simpler and matches the RDF 4D semantics (fact + time range).

related.why: Entity system provides disambiguation and name normalization; KG queries rely on entity_id canonicalization
KG is one pillar of MemPalace architecture alongside vector search and palace rooms; explains system topology
MCP server exposes tool_kg_* functions; manages per-path KG caching and provides the public interface

searchDoc.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph
searchDoc.summary: The Temporal Knowledge Graph stores structured facts as subject-predicate-object triples with optional valid_from/valid_to timestamps, enabling queries at specific points in time. Built on local SQLite with thread-safe WAL mode and no external dependencies, it complements vector search with deterministic relationship queries and serves as ground truth for fact-checking and entity disambiguation.
searchDoc.body: The MemPalace Temporal Knowledge Graph stores structured facts as subject-predicate-object triples (RDF style) with optional valid_from and valid_to timestamps, so callers can ask what was true at a specific instant. It is built on a single local SQLite database at ~/.mempalace/knowledge_graph.sqlite3 with Write-Ahead Logging for durability and concurrent reads, zero external dependencies, and no subscriptions. A threading lock guards every database operation; the connection uses check_same_thread False and a 10-second busy timeout. Each KnowledgeGraph instance is a singleton per palace path, cached in mcp_server._kg_by_path so there is a single writer and consistent reads. The schema has two tables: entities (id, name, type, properties JSON) and triples (subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_to, confidence, provenance fields) with indexes on subject, object, predicate, and the temporal columns. Temporal values accept both legacy date-only YYYY-MM-DD and canonical UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ formats. Date-only values are normalized at query time via SQL CASE expressions: valid_from becomes T00:00:00Z and valid_to becomes T23:59:59Z, so a date is treated as a full 24-hour window and as_of queries with canonical UTC datetimes still match older facts. The _temporal_filter_sql function assembles the WHERE clause. add_triple auto-creates missing entity nodes, normalizes the predicate to lowercase with underscores, generates a unique triple_id from a hash of valid_from and the current timestamp, validates that valid_to is not before valid_from (raising ValueError on an inverted interval, which would otherwise be invisible to every query), and deduplicates identical open triples. query_entity reads facts in three directions: outgoing, incoming, or both, joining entity names. invalidate closes a fact by setting valid_to and is idempotent, finding only triples with valid_to IS NULL. The KG does not enforce referential integrity at write time; the foreign key on subject is a soft constraint because entities are auto-created. timeline returns up to 100 facts chronologically. The KG is ground truth for fact_checker.py contradiction and name-confusion detection and for entity_registry.py disambiguation, and is ingested by project and conversation miners through adapters carrying RFC 002 section 5.5 provenance. SQLite was chosen over Neo4j for a local-first, zero external API design.
